Welcome from our Head of School
Welcome to Primrose Lane Primary School, part of the Yeovil Area Community Academy Trust (YACAT). Our aim is for all children to reach their full potential and to be equipped to embrace their future. Our curriculum and extra-curricular activities ensure that the children are able to develop into confident learners. The staff are a dedicated and hard-working team who always put children at the heart of their decisions in order to ensure that the children are confident, happy and safe. We recognise the importance of good relationships with parents and carers and we welcome a close and open relationship with you all. I hope that this website provides you with all the information you need but we also welcome visits in order for you to really get a feel for the school. Mrs A Sherrard Head of School

pageCache.pageTitle: Primrose Lane Primary School - Welcome to Little Learners
pageCache.text:
Little Learners Pre-School
PROVISION FOR 2-4 YEAR OLDS
Welcome to Little Learners Pre-School at Primrose Lane, where we offer a warm, friendly, stimulating environment for children aged 2-4 years old.
Throughout the week the children enjoy a range of exciting balanced activities from; letters and sounds, cooking, outdoor play and lots more. Our blog page is regularly updated to show some of the fun we have.
We spend lots of time outside exploring our surroundings and the elements. We also join in with relevant school events such as Remembrance Day and assemblies.
Our Opening hours are from 8am to 4pm (term time only) and we offer the following sessions
8 am-4 pm; 8 am-1 pm; 1 pm-4 pm
APPLYING FOR A PLACE
To apply for a place, click on the link below to download a Registration Form, or you can collect a copy from the school office.
The majority of places become available from September each year and are allocated during the summer term. We will be allocating places for September 2026 at the end of April / beginning of May 2026. Any applications received after this initial allocation will be considered on a first come, first served basis subject to availability.
Spaces at Little Learners are limited (particularly for 2 year olds) and, whilst we will endeavour to offer places to as many children as possible, submitting a Registration Form does not guarantee a place.
Places will be allocated in accordance with our Admissions Policy.
**Please note that attending Little Learners Pre-School does not give any priority for a place at Primrose Lane Primary School**
Little Learners is based in a dedicated classroom within Primrose Lane Primary School. As well as this space we have a wooden cabin which we use for small group work and some lovely outdoor spaces which we use as much as possible, including a garden area.
Each day we follow a daily routine but this can be adjusted based on planned activities like walks, PE sessions or the children's interests.
We deliver the learning curriculum through themed activities - an example of a half-termly theme plan can be found below.
We work on letters and sounds with the children daily and further details regarding learning and the curriculum can be found on the Little Learners Learning and Development page.
Children attending morning or full day sessions will have lunch at Little Learners. You may either provide a home packed lunch, or order and pay for a Meal via the school meals payment system “My Child at School” ( Login details and instructions will be provided after your child has started at Little Learners). School Meals for Little Learners are charged at £2.25 per day. All charges are payable in advance and meals must be booked by the Tuesday of the week before the meal is to be taken.
Click here for Apr 2026 / Oct 2026 Hot School Meals Menu
If sending in a packed lunch, please be aware we do not heat up any food and your child’s packed lunch will need to contain an ice pack.
Primrose Lane Primary School is a nut free environment so please ensure that no nuts or items including nuts are sent in lunchboxes (e.g. pesto pasta, chocolate hazelnut spread or bakewell tarts).
If your child will be attending in the morning and you would like them to have breakfast at Little Learners, we can provide this for £1 per day. This must be booked and paid for half-termly in advance.
If your child still uses nappies when they start at Little Learners, you will need to provide these (together with any cream if needed).
Our hourly fees from September 2026 are:
2 year old hourly rate: £7.00 per hour
3 & 4 year old hourly rate: £6.00 per hour
Little Learners has set session times as follows:
We have a minimum booking of 2 sessions a week (8.00am - 4.00pm counts as 2 sessions).
Fees are invoiced half-termly in advance and are payable as per our Fees Policy.
Little Learners accepts the Early Years Entitlement funding from Somerset Council (Universal funding for 3 and 4 year olds, Supported funding for eligible 2 year olds and Working Parent Funding for eligible families).
We claim any relevant funding directly from the Council and invoice parents for any unfunded hours.
For more information about funding and to check eligibility visit: https://www.beststartinlife.gov.uk/childcare-early-years-education
Further information about Little Learners can be found in our prospectus.

pageCache.text:
British Values
The Department for Education has published guidance to schools on promoting British values to prepare young people for life in modern Britain. At Primrose Lane Primary School we take this responsibility very seriously and we actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs.
These concepts are explored through our curriculum and in all subjects but in Religious Education and PSHE and Citizenship, in particular, where children can deepen their understanding. We make great efforts to ensure our children are exposed to a wide range of experiences beyond their own community.
DEMOCRACY
'Democracy and Freedom are dreams you never give up’.
At Primrose Lane Primary school we listen to the views of children and we do this through a variety of means including:
Pupil surveys
Assemblies
Circle time
THE RULE OF THE LAW
'True freedom requires the rule of law and justice, and a judicial system in which the rights of some are not secured by the denial of rights to others’.
Chief Rabbi, Jonathan Sacks
Our school has ‘Golden Rules’ which promote the well-being of the individual and the school as a whole. Each class reinforces those rules and they are a central part of the school ethos. They include being kind, helpful, fair and polite to everyone in our school; look after and take care of things around us; try hard to do our best in everything we do. The school has a positive behaviour policy that sets out rewards and sanctions. We encourage children to recognise rights and how these go hand in hand with responsibility
INDIVIDUAL LIBERTY
‘One child, one teacher, one book, and one pen, can change the world.’
We support children to make informed choices in a secure setting. Children develop self-respect and value themselves as individuals. Our school ethos, and methods of teaching, develop children’s independence as well as other qualities such as perseverance and resilience.
Children are encouraged to achieve highly and work hard. Through determination and self belief we foster ambition. Visits from doctors, surgeons, solicitors and politicians encourage all children to follow their dreams and to develop plans towards fulfilling their career goals.
Mutual Respect
‘We must learn to live together as brothers and sisters, or we will perish together as fools’.
Martin Luther King, Jr.
Respect is a core value of our school and underpins our ethos. Respect is shown by all adults and children towards each other and towards our community. Our wide and broad curriculum supports this and helps children to articulate what respect means in practice. Children can talk about their own faith and beliefs as well as the faiths and beliefs of others. Our emphasis is one of unity around what unites us as human beings.
TOLERANCE OF THOSE WITH DIFFERENT FAITHS AND BELIEFS
‘The highest result of education is tolerance’
Through Religious Education and PSHE and Citizenship, in particular, we deepen children’s understanding of faith and belief. We participate in a wide range of celebrations such as Chinese New Year, Diwali, Eid, Christmas and Guru Nanak’s birthday as well as many others. We welcome visitors from our community and those beyond. We have an emphasis on British culture and celebrate St George’s day and Shakespeare’s birthday on the 23rd of April .
At Primrose Lane Primary School, we view these fundamental British values as universal moral beliefs that are commonly held across the world. We teach these through a distinct curriculum that recognises the unique culture of Britain whilst developing in our pupils a pride in being part of the British nation
"Not every child has an equal talent or an equal ability or equal motivation, but they should have the equal right to develop their talent and their ability and their motivation, to make something of themselves.” ​

pageCache.text:
Primrose Lane Vision and Values
At Primrose Lane all children and staff hold the golden rules at the very heart of everything that we do.
YACAT Vision and Values
OUR VISION
For all children within our family of schools to have access to learning and experiences that allow them to be confident and ambitious, to realise their potential, and to believe in their own success.
For each school within our trust to thrive and grow, to build and nurture a strong identity within its own community.
OUR VALUES
Teamwork
Teamwork in our trust starts with the children, who are taught the skills and benefits of collaboration throughout their primary journey. Opportunities to work together are found through the taught and broader curriculum. Schools in our trust, and their continued success, are reliant on the collective efforts of our staff team and parents working together to create school environments that nurture growth, learning, and personal development.
Aspiration
We want our children to be ambitious about the possibilities for themselves now and in the future, to believe that they can go beyond the expected, to refuse to be limited in what their lives can bring. Schools in our trust are reflective and always seeking to improve. We believe that by working together, all schools can improve and should strive to do so. Our schools are ambitious for their children and view overcoming disadvantage as key.
Kindness
Kindness is the cornerstone of community. We work hard to help our children to value kindness and to become thoughtful, compassionate individuals who embrace difference and do the right thing even when no one is watching.We expect children, staff and parents to be thoughtful and considerate towards one another and to build positive relationships: to be kind and respectful in their interactions.
Success
We believe that it is our role to enable all children to succeed. Through our curriculum, broader offer and partnerships, we strive for all to reach their potential. Success for schools in our trust builds on strong foundations in reading, writing and maths; to encompass other taught subjects, wider personal development, becoming a responsible member of the community and preparation for secondary school. Through effective partnership, working schools in our trust are supported to succeed, to improve outcomes for the children in their care, and to meet their wider goals.

Breakfast Club
The Breakfast Club aims
Start Time
The breakfast club is held in the Hall with doors opening at 8:00am with the session running from 8:00am until 8:40am.
Drop Off
Parents are welcome to drop their children off any time between 8:00am and 8:30am. Please bring your child to the side doors in the Hall.
Parking
If needed, please use the drop off parking area.
The Breakfast Club will provide:-
A healthy breakfast including cereal, toast and a drink.
A choice of activity after breakfast such as table top games, drawing, reading will provide a calm atmosphere where children can relax ready for for the day ahead.
Cost
The cost is £3.60 per session. BACS and Childcare vouchers are accepted.
Missed Sessions
We regret that any absences will not be refunded and it is your reponsibility to cancel any upcoming bookings.
How do I book?
All bookings are to be made via MCAS 48 hours prior to sessions needed. Please click on the days you need and pay the correct amount. If you need to book your child in within the 48 hour cut off please contact the school office.

After School Care
"Premier Education is a local organisation that works closely with schools to support families by delivering high-quality Afterschool Club provision. Our wraparound care offers children a safe, engaging, and enjoyable start and end to their school day".
At our clubs, children take part in a wide range of activities, including daily sports sessions led by fully qualified and compliant coaches. Sporting activities vary each day, giving children the opportunity to try new skills and stay active.
Alongside sport, children can enjoy a variety of creative craft activities, with a new theme each week inspired by popular children’s books. These themed sessions encourage children to explore different techniques, spark their imagination, and develop their creativity.
Children attending Full Afterschool Club sessions are also provided with a variety of balanced, nutritious snacks to keep them energised throughout the session.
We are also Ofsted registered and allow all types of childcare vouchers.
We’re proud to support the school community and look forward to continuing to work with families and children throughout the year.

We aim to make the children at PLPS confident and happy learners and to equip them with the skills to make the right choices in later life empowering them to be active and responsible citizens.
We also aim to ensure that the children of PLPS recognise and embrace the diversity of the world we live in. At Primrose Lane we give the children the confidence, skills and knowledge to develop sustainable relationships with others and also ensure that they understand how their bodies change over time.
All the classes use the Coram Life curriculum plans.

Little Learners Learning and Development
CURRICULUM AND PLANNING
Little Learners follows the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum. We deliver this curriculum through a range of activities which seek to develop children's skills, knowledge and understanding in a themed and play-based environment.
Click here to view the Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework
We use "Development Matters" to track the children's progress within the EYFS.
Click here to view the Development Matters Tracker
We operate a three year curriculum theme plan. This is subject to change due to children's interests and real world events.
Little Learners 3 year Curriculum Plan
Within each theme, we plan a range of activities which deliver the various areas of the curriculum through stories, crafts, themed free play and adult led activities. We cover Letters and Sounds every day and Mathematics is woven through our curriculum activities.
Below is an example of a planning template showing how we take a curriculum theme and structure our plan of activities around this, together with some photographs of how this theme was delivered in the Pre-School setting.

YOUR CHILD'S PROGRESS
The Little Learners staff make observations of the way your child engages in the activities to track and record their development and to develop next steps to enable them to progress. We send home a booklet showing your child's Learning Journey each term and offer two Parent Meetings with your child's keyworker each year.

Geography
OUR VISION
From the moment we are born, it is our instinct to begin to explore our world around us with all our senses.
At Primrose Lane we feel it is important to nurture and encourage that natural curiosity, to shape and direct it to turn the children into inquisitive, questioning learners who look closely at the world around them and begin to be able to interpret what they see. As a whole school we look at countries around the world and learn about the similarities and differences between British culture and others.
In Little Learners and Red Class (Reception), Geography comes under the curriculum area of ‘Understanding the World,’ providing links with science and history. We encourage the children to explore our outdoor area and investigate the plants and animals that we find there – we draw them, label them, research them, make homes for them and follow the children’s interests in learning more about them. We introduce the beginnings of map work, encouraging children to look closely at what they see and to draw it accurately.
At Primrose Lane we also aim to instil in children a sense of environmental responsibility and encourage them to understand environmental issues at a local and global level.
Running through all of our Geography work at Primrose Lane is the idea that we are motivating and inspiring our children to find out about their world, both physical and human, so that they can take an active part in contributing to and protecting this world as they grow up.

Music
“Music produces a kind of pleasure which human nature cannot do without.”
“How is it that music can, without words, evoke our laughter, our fears, our highest aspirations?”
OUR VISION
Our curriculum allows for all children to access a wide range of musical genres, styles and periods through listening and participation. The genres we cover are wide reaching and include World Music and music with a purpose. Within the Foundation Stage, music is a helpful basis to teach through phonic songs, nursery rhymes and counting songs.
Skills of musical analysis and description are built on progressively throughout the school, creating a thorough knowledge of the inter-related dimensions of music including pitch, tempo, dynamics, texture, timbre, duration and structure. Alongside this, we teach musical notations, allowing children to understand how songs are created in written form.
The main aim of music at Primrose is enjoyment and inclusivity. Everyone can participate in music and we want to give children the confidence to try, participate and succeed within this creative world. Music is remarkable and we want to pass the enjoyment that can be felt around music onto our children which they can carry throughout their lives.

Attendance
THE IMPORTANCE OF ATTENDANCE
Pupils who are taken out of school during term time may find it hard to catch up and this can have a detrimental effect on their learning.
The law states that parents DO NOT have the right to take their children out of school for holidays during term time. We would like to remind you that any request for Term Time Leave must be made in writing to the Head Teacher in advance by using one of the Leave of Absence request forms found in reception. (Requests will not usually be granted and will only be authorised in EXCEPTIONAL circumstances according to DfE guidelines).
Any unauthorised absence, including term time leave not agreed with the school, could result in a Warning Penalty Notice being issued to each parent for every child affected.Our attendance Policy states that we have a whole school expectation of 97.5%.
